stem: Who was first to use the characteristics of vascular tissues in the classification of plants?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: A.P. de Candolle (Augustin Pyramus de Candolle) was a Swiss botanist, who coined the word “taxonomy” for the first time and developed a natural system of plant classification. The systematic use of characteristics of vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) in plant classification was first done by A.P. de Candolle.

stem: Which of the following is an example of the binomial scientific name?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Under the binomial nomenclature system, the name of a species consists of two parts. The first part is the genus name and the second part is the species name. In the above question, Rana tigrina is the scientific name of a frog. Therefore, it is an example of a binomial scientific name.

stem: Protista group includes–
expl: All unicellular eukaryotic organisms are included in the Protista group. Heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms are included in the Animal Kingdom, and all green plants are included in the Plant Kingdom.

stem: in lichen, a chlorophyll-containing partner, __________ live together.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In lichens, a chlorophyll-containing partner—algae (phycobiont)—and a chlorophyll-lacking partner—fungus (mycobiont)—live together. This is called mutualism. In this type of association, the fungus is the more dominant partner. The fungus provides shelter, water, and minerals to the algae, and in return, the algae provides food to the fungus, which it prepares through photosynthesis. In lichens, reproduction occurs through the fungal component. In biology, when two organisms help each other, it is called a symbiotic (Mutualism) relationship.

stem: Choose the vascular plant from the following:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Fern is a non-flowering vascular plant. Vascular plants are those plants in which lignified tissues such as xylem and phloem are present to carry water and minerals from the soil to different parts of the plant.

stem: in mycorrhizal association, the advantage of plant is :

options.label: d
options.text: Increased mineral absorption and disease protection

expl: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association formed between certain fungi and the roots of higher plants. In this association, the plant especially benefits through increased absorption of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other micronutrients. Plants with mycorrhiza also get protection from root-borne diseases and some harmful soil microorganisms.

stem: Spirogyra is an example of which of the following algae?
expl: Spirogyra is an example of green algae. It contains chlorophyll; therefore, it makes its own food through photosynthesis. There are more than 400 species of Spirogyra worldwide. Spirogyra is also called water silk.

stem: Which of the following is an example of algae ?
expl: Diatoms are unicellular algae. They are organisms found on Earth that have a cell wall made of transparent, opaline silica. They belong to the kingdom Protista.

stem: Which of the following is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom?
expl: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom. Among all species found on Earth, nearly two-thirds of the species belong to Arthropoda.

stem: What is true for phylum echinodermata?

options.label: a
options.text: They are triploblastic and have coelomic cavity.

options.label: b
options.text: They have a peculiar water-driven tube system.

options.label: c
options.text: They are exclusively free living marine animals.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Phylum Echinodermata: They are exclusively marine organisms. They are multicellular animals with well-developed organ systems. Most echinoderms are star-shaped and have a cylindrical body form. They are triploblastic and possess a coelomic cavity. They also have a characteristic water vascular system. They respire through tube feet and dermal bronchiae (skin gills).

stem: The animal without red blood cells is –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Earthworm lacks red blood corpuscles. However, an earthworm appears red because haemoglobin is dissolved in its plasma.

stem: The smallest organism, capable of autonomous growth and reproduction, is
expl: Mycoplasma is the smallest organism that can grow and reproduce autonomously (Self-replicating).

stem: Fungi are plants that lack –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Chlorophyll is not found in fungi. For various reasons, fungi are no longer placed in the plant kingdom. Earlier they were included under plants, but fungi are not plants; they belong to a separate kingdom.

stem: After bringing out of water fishes die, because-

options.label: a
options.text: They get excess quantity of oxygen

options.label: d
options.text: They can not move in water

expl: When fish are taken out of water, they die because they cannot breathe. Fish have gills, which are mainly adapted to absorb oxygen (O) dissolved in water.

stem: How do the members of honey-bee hive recognise each-other?
expl: Almost all animals have methods of exchanging information. They communicate through sight, sound, touch and smell. Honeybees perform different dance patterns to indicate the direction of food and the location of its source, while they recognize each other by smell. These smell-based chemicals are pheromones.

stem: Dolphins are classified as –
expl: Dolphins are aquatic mammals. Many subspecies of dolphins are found; among them, the Ganga river dolphin is India’s National Aquatic Animal.

stem: Frogs and toads are examples of which of the following amphibians?
expl: Frog and toad are examples of amphibians of the order Anura. Major features of Anura include: they have four limbs; their hind limbs are longer and stronger than the forelimbs, which helps them in jumping.

stem: Does a bryophyte have a spore mother cell?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In bryophytes, the spore mother cell is diploid. Bryophytes include mosses and liverworts, which are generally found in moist and shady regions of hilly areas. Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.

stem: What is the structural and functional unit of life?
expl: All living organisms are made up of cells. Some organisms are made of a single cell; they are called unicellular organisms, such as protozoa, Euglena, etc. Organisms like humans, which are made up of many cells, are called multicellular organisms. A unicellular organism can exist independently and perform essential life processes. Anything smaller than a cell cannot ensure independent existence; therefore, the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living beings.

stem: The powerhouse of the cell is -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Mitochondria are double-membrane-bound organelles scattered in the cytoplasm of all living plant and animal cells, except bacteria and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria). They are called the powerhouse of the cell because complete oxidation of glucose takes place in them. Hence, mitochondria are the power source of the cell.

stem: Which of the following does not have any enzyme in its cells?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The word “virus” is derived from the Latin word “virus”, which literally means poison or sticky liquid. Viruses are acellular, ultramicroscopic organisms that can multiply only inside a living cell. Generally, enzymes are absent in viruses; however, some viruses such as retroviruses contain certain enzymes. Chemically, a virus is a segment of nucleic acid surrounded by a protein coat. Outside the host cell, viruses can neither perform any biological activity nor replicate. Enzymes are also present in lichen, bacteria, and algae.

stem: The substance found in more than 80% of the cell is :
expl: Water is present in the maximum amount in a cell. Water is the most abundant substance in cells and is about 70% or more of the total cell mass. Therefore, option (d) can be selected as the nearest answer.

stem: Which of the following is found both in the cells of a mango plant and a monkey?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In the above question, the cell membrane is found in the cells of both the mango plant and the monkey. The cell membrane is semipermeable. It separates the internal part of the cell from the external environment and also provides structural support to the cell.

stem: Which of the following statements about permanent tissues is correct?

options.label: a
options.text: They are capable of rapid cell division

options.label: b
options.text: They are found only in young plants

options.label: c
options.text: They lose the ability to divide

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The tissues that are fully developed and have lost the ability to divide are called permanent tissues. Hence, option (c) is correct.

stem: Plants and animal cells differ in which of the following structure?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Plant cells have a cell wall along with a cell membrane. In plants, the cell wall surrounds the cell membrane. It gives a definite shape to the plant cell. Animal cells have a cell membrane, but they do not have a cell wall.
